prompt: AiDot RGBW lights (A21 RGBTW Wi-Fi bulbs) in the built-in AiDot integration do not apply the requested RGBW color when brightness and an RGBW color are sent together in one light turn-on action. The brightness changes, but the bulb keeps the color it had before. This is most visible with scenes: when a scene is activated, the brightness changes correctly but the color does not. Changing the color by hand works, sending only an RGBW color in the turn-on action works, and sending only brightness works. For example, a turn-on action with brightness 128 and RGBW color 0, 0, 255, 0 changes the brightness, but the light does not turn blue. No error is logged and the action succeeds. The reporter thinks the integration treats brightness, color temperature and RGBW color as alternatives, with brightness checked first, so the color is dropped whenever brightness is present. Brightness should be applied independently of the color setting, so that one turn-on action applies both the brightness and the color. Seen on Home Assistant Core 2026.8.3 (Home Assistant OS); the earlier custom AiDot integration worked.
AiDot lights ignore the RGBW color or color temperature when brightness is sent in the same turn-on action, for example from a scene. Apply both.

Shelly firmware 2.0.0 added an Advanced Security setting on the device. Shelly devices made before that do not ship with a built-in HTTPS certificate. So a user can turn Advanced Security on and never upload an HTTPS certificate, for example to stay compatible with other third-party systems. The device's own setup popup says that HTTPS access works only when an HTTPS server certificate is uploaded, and that without a certificate the device keeps working normally over HTTP. Home Assistant always assumes that HTTPS is in use when Advanced Security is on for a Shelly device. Because of this, the HTTP port (80) that was correctly discovered for the device is silently replaced. Home Assistant should not assume HTTPS only because Advanced Security is on, and should keep the port it found. Seen on Home Assistant Core 2026.8.2, Home Assistant OS.
Shelly devices with Advanced Security on but no HTTPS certificate get their HTTP port 80 silently replaced; stop assuming HTTPS and keep the real port.

With the SwitchBot Cloud integration, a SwitchBot air purifier that is unplugged reports a mode value of 0. While it is unplugged, the Home Assistant log keeps filling with an error about this mode value 0 on every update, because the integration cannot turn it into one of the purifier's modes. The integration should handle this mode value without the error. Seen on Home Assistant Core 2026.7.2, Home Assistant OS.
An unplugged SwitchBot air purifier reports mode 0, and the SwitchBot Cloud integration logs an error on every update. Handle that mode without the error.

With the IKEA TRADFRI integration, one TRADFRI remote control for a while returned its device information without the firmware version. When the integration was then reloaded, setup of the whole sensor platform failed with a missing-key error, and every TRADFRI battery sensor became unavailable. The IKEA app and the gateway kept working, and all lights and the control outlet stayed controllable. The IKEA app showed that remote without a firmware version. After the remote was woken or power-cycled, its firmware version appeared again, and a reload of the integration brought back all battery sensors. Steps: have a TRADFRI battery device for which the gateway leaves out the firmware version, reload the integration, and see that all TRADFRI battery sensors become unavailable. The integration should tolerate a missing firmware version for one device, for example by leaving that device's firmware version empty, instead of failing setup of every entity of that platform. Seen on Home Assistant Core 2026.8.3, Home Assistant OS 18.2, gateway firmware 1.21.57, 16 devices on the gateway.
If one IKEA TRADFRI remote reports no firmware version, all TRADFRI battery sensors fail to set up. Tolerate it and leave that device's firmware version empty.

Since Supervisor 2026.03.3, Home Assistant backups contain one more inner archive, supervisor.tar.gz (or supervisor.tar), with the Supervisor's own configuration: the network storage mounts and the Docker registry settings. It is encrypted like the other inner archives. When Core rewrites a backup, it decrypts or encrypts the inner archives, but it copies this one through unchanged, while it changes the backup metadata to say that the backup is now encrypted or not encrypted. This happens whenever Core rewrites a backup: for example when it uploads a backup to Supervisor backup locations with mixed encryption settings, or when a user downloads a decrypted backup. On restore, the Supervisor opens the archive as the metadata says and fails: a backup that Core decrypted still holds the encrypted configuration archive, and a backup that Core encrypted still holds it in plain form. The Supervisor hides the failure, and the network storage mounts are silently not restored. A separate Supervisor bug also breaks this restore, but this Core fault would still break it after that bug is fixed. Core should decrypt and encrypt the Supervisor configuration archive in the same way as the other inner archives when it rewrites a backup.

When Core decrypts or encrypts a backup, the inner Supervisor configuration archive (supervisor.tar.gz) is left unchanged, so network mounts are not restored. Process it like the other inner archives.

When the Kodi integration fails to send a notification to Kodi, it catches the error and only writes it to the log. The user gets no feedback in the UI that the action failed, and automations go on as if the action worked. Change this so that a failure to send the notification makes the action fail with an error that the user sees, instead of only being logged. The error should use a translated message, added to the integration's translations. After the fix, remove the comment that tells the linter to accept the old handling.
When sending a Kodi notification fails, the error is only logged. Make the action fail with a translated error the user sees instead.

In the Hive integration, setup only sets up the device types (lights, switches, sensors, binary sensors, heating, water heater) for which the account has devices, but unload always tries to unload all of them. This mismatch has two separate effects. First, Hive's own heating and hot water actions exist only when the account has such devices. So for an account that returns no water heater device, the hot water action never exists, and automations that call it fail because the action does not exist, with no other sign. Which actions exist should not depend on which devices were found. Second, a reload fails for any account that lacks one device type. On an account with no Hive bulbs, unloading the lights fails with an error. The entry is left broken, Home Assistant refuses to reload it, and the integration stays dead until a full restart. Reproduced on Home Assistant Core 2026.9.3 with an account that had no lights. A change in Core turns this unload failure into a warning, but then every reload warns for the common case of a user with no Hive bulbs or smart plugs. The reporter suggests remembering which device types were set up and unloading exactly those. Always setting up every device type is not safe as it is: the other device types handle an empty device list, but setting up the binary sensors fails when the account data has no binary sensor entry at all, rather than an empty one. Both effects should be fixed: the actions exist without matching devices, and a reload succeeds.
With no Hive devices of some type, Hive's own heating and hot water actions never exist and reloading the integration fails. Make both work without those devices.

I have an Atlantic Optimocosy HR plus ventilation unit that I connect to Home Assistant through a TaHoma Switch, using the hub's local API. The ventilation works well, and all its sensors show up and work. But I cannot change anything on the ventilation, because its control entity appears unavailable. The log shows an error that happens because one state value of the device is missing: with the local API, the hub does not report that state for this unit. Home Assistant should handle the missing state, so that the ventilation control is available and I can change its settings. I use Home Assistant Core 2026.9.1 on Home Assistant OS. I do not know a last working version.
My Atlantic ventilation unit on a TaHoma Switch (local API) shows as unavailable and cannot be controlled, because one device state is missing. Please fix it.

I paired HomeKit accessories with Home Assistant, and I exported the diagnostics download for one of them. The diagnostics do not hide internal IP addresses in a consistent way. In the data section of the entry, the field with the accessory's single IP address is redacted. But right after it there is a list that still shows the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of the device in clear text: an internal IPv4 address, an address with my ISP's IPv6 prefix, and an address with a ULA IPv6 prefix. Maybe this only happens on IPv6 networks. The list of addresses should be redacted in the same way as the single address. I use Home Assistant Core 2026.9.2 on Home Assistant OS.
HomeKit accessory diagnostics redact the single IP address but still show a separate list of the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. Please redact that list too.

I have a devolo Magic 1 WiFi 2-1 (MT 3133, firmware 6.0.1) in Home Assistant. Each time the integration sets up the device, so at every Home Assistant start, Home Assistant asks the device for a scan of the Wi-Fi networks in range. It does this even when the sensor that shows those other networks is disabled, which is its default. The scan takes about 8.5 seconds, and sensitive Wi-Fi clients lose their connection to the access point when it finishes. In my case the Wi-Fi dongle of a GoodWe inverter (a Hi-Flying module) dropped off the network about 90 seconds after every start, at the moment the scan result came back. A packet capture showed this, and three restarts in a row gave the same failure, 97 to 105 seconds after the start. The other data that Home Assistant reads from the device comes back within 50 to 500 ms and causes no problem. When I disabled the devolo entry, the next restart did not disconnect the client. The scan runs only once at setup; it does not repeat after that, because nothing uses its data. Since the sensor is disabled by default, no scan should run unless a user enables the sensor. Home Assistant Core 2026.9.4, Home Assistant OS 18.3.
Every Home Assistant start makes my devolo Wi-Fi adapter scan for nearby networks, even with that sensor disabled, and clients disconnect. Only scan when the sensor is enabled.

I have two Imou IPC-C22F-C cameras that I add to Home Assistant over ONVIF. The cameras have only a Wi-Fi connection, but over ONVIF each one reports two MAC addresses. The first is a common address that is the same on both cameras, 00:30:1B:BA:02:DB (maybe for an Ethernet port that does not exist; a web search shows it is a common Dahua MAC address). The second is the MAC address of the Wi-Fi adapter, which is different on each camera. Home Assistant takes only the first, common MAC address. When I add the first camera, it gets a new device whose name ends with "- 00:30:1b:ba:02:db". When I try to add the second camera, Home Assistant treats it as the camera that is already set up and puts it under the same device as the first one, so I cannot remove one camera without removing both. Each camera should be identified by its own Wi-Fi MAC address, so that the second camera is added as a separate device. Home Assistant Core 2026.1.3 on Home Assistant OS.
Two Imou ONVIF cameras report the same first MAC address, so the second one cannot be added separately. Use each camera's own Wi-Fi MAC address instead.
